claim: The Na SXRD reflections persist through discharge/charge with only modest intensity loss.
The crystalline oxide phase of PCO is largely retained during sodiation.
No metallic Co phase forms during discharge/charge.
SXRD probes crystallographic/phase-fraction change in the material.
The Na SAXS contours stay nearly straight and I(q) curves overlap except a small drop near q~0.03-0.1 A-1 at 0.11/0.02 V.
The pore structure of Na/PCO is barely altered over the first cycle.
SAXS probes nanoscale porosity/morphology change in the material.
Neither technique alone constrains the other's structural aspect (crystallographic vs. porosity).
PCO undergoes only slight sodiation-driven change overall, spanning both lattice and pore-network levels.
Both observations together are needed to support that PCO stays structurally intact at both the lattice and pore-network level during the first cycle.
